entries.text: Your ledger closes in wet tallow and dried blood; the Salt Tithe claims another unpaid name.
Cold iron slips from numb fingers while crows gather above the silent tollhouse.
No lantern answers from the river ford. Only silt and drifting ash mark where the company stood.
Under Third-Dynasty Probate Law, a fallen debtor's ribs belong to the next bailiff who passes.
The wardstone hum fades in your ears, replaced by the slow drip of groundwater on rusted mail.
Shaved silver groats spill across the mud—worthless now to the hand that counted them.
Your bowstring snaps in the sleet, and the treeline closes around the last standing banner.
The telluric valve ruptures without a ground; ozone and cinder swallow the final invocation.
A cracked helmet rolls into the drainage ditch, leaving the Alder Bridge unguarded until dawn.
No quartermaster will tally this loss; the Border Mint burned cleaner records than your bones.
Alkali dust fills your visor as the desert wind erases every bootprint behind the caravan.
Ironheart's sluice-gates stay bolted shut while your company bleeds out onto dry limestone.
Whale-oil slicks catch the last spark, turning the harbor stones into a smoking pyre.
The tide rises through the Sunken Citadel, sealing helm and cuirass beneath cold black brine.
Your grounding rod snaps under the surge, and the storm leaves nothing but vitrified glass.
Caldera ash settles thick over fallen shields, burying steel and oath alike before nightfall.
Even star-iron bends when the hammer falls too late; the Obsidian Dais claims its toll.
The Anchor Seals groan deeper beneath the sea, indifferent to one more broken vanguard.
A cold draft extinguishes the camp brazier. Tomorrow another sellsword will take your contract.
Bitumen and copper wire await the unclaimed dead—pray the Scriptorium never finds your corpse.
Your last healing phial shatters on stone; the red stain dries faster than winter rain.
None of the Twelve walked out of that gorge. Only silence returns to the watch-post.
The road to Ironcamp is paved with better captains than you—and none of them turned back either.
Venom turns the blood to marsh-silt before a single prayer can reach the dry air.
Your name is struck from the muster roll with a blunt thumb of charcoal.
Steel rings once against basalt, then only the wind through empty ribcages remains.
The fog drinks the torchlight whole, leaving the frontier one company poorer.
No bell tolls in Thornwick for mercenaries who die beyond the outer palisade.
Your shield-arm drops; the breach widens; the chronicle ends mid-sentence.
Ashkarath's furnace does not mourn its fuel. Rise again, if any silver remains to buy steel.
